title: Linus Pauling's 1931 paper "The nature of the chemical bond"
summary: Pauling's April 1931 JACS article set out six rules for the shared-electron bond, the last three of them new, derived from quantum mechanics and a theory of paramagnetic susceptibility.
body: Linus Pauling's article in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, volume 53 (April 1931), pages 1367-1400, treated the shared-electron bond with quantum mechanics. The Crossref record for DOI 10.1021/ja01355a027 registers the title as "THE NATURE OF THE CHEMICAL BOND. APPLICATION OF RESULTS OBTAINED FROM THE QUANTUM MECHANICS AND FROM A THEORY OF PARAMAGNETIC SUSCEPTIBILITY TO THE STRUCTURE OF MOLECULES", issued April 1931. Oregon State University's archive of the Pauling papers dates the submitted typescript 17 February 1931 and states that the paper "presented six rules for the shared electron bond", the last three new, among them that the orbital overlapping most with another atom's orbital would form the strongest bond, the bond tending to lie in that direction. The archive also quotes Pauling in the paper: "even the formal justification of the electron-pair bond in the simplest cases. . . requires a formidable array of symbols and equations."
